answer: An operator rotating funds across many keys therefore bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never pays. Because the wharf fee is applied at the dawn exit, the plume audit totals the burn and the ledger shows exactly what left. Withdrawing stake burns a 9% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. That is 18 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
